clue.text: Tudor's defeat by Gloucester?

indicators.note: a defeated side is broken and scattered, so the letters of the name are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about some battle in which a Tudor army was beaten by the Duke of Gloucester.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'Tudor's' counts as a letter here. 'Gloucester' looks like the victorious duke, but the definition places the answer near the city: STROUD is a Gloucestershire town a few miles away.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroud is a market town lying close to the cathedral city in western England, hence the question mark.

clue.text: 25 22's child pupil in stature to accommodate

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: in puts the learner inside the word for stature

parts.note: stature is height
L for learner
to house is to accommodate

explanation.surface: Woolf's small pupil grows in size to fit in.
explanation.definitionFit: To the Lighthouse is a 1927 novel by the writer, set on Skye.

clue.text: 25 22's golden country with love

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a land is a country
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Woolf's golden land is full of love.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando is a 1928 novel by the writer about a hero who changes sex over centuries.

clue.text: Ballet master, fat in face, taking two fifths

indicators.note: in puts the fat inside the clock face

parts.note: a dial is a clock face
ghi is a variant spelling of ghee, clarified butter
E is the fifth letter of the alphabet
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A plump-faced ballet impresario helps himself to two fifths of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking two fifths' adds two different fives: E, fifth letter of the alphabet, and V, the Roman five.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergei Diaghilev was the impresario who founded the Ballets Russes.

clue.text: Cryptographer keeps caliph to say what's right

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so the code inventor's name wraps around the ruler

parts.note: Samuel Morse devised the Morse code, loosely a cryptographer
Ali was the fourth caliph of Islam

explanation.surface: A codebreaker takes a Muslim ruler under his wing in order to lecture on ethics.
explanation.definitionFit: To moralise is to pronounce on right and wrong conduct, often preachily.

clue.text: Crazy about true reform that's now ready

indicators.note: about means the crazy word goes round the rest

parts.note: mad means crazy

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape, so these letters are recast

explanation.surface: Fanatical about genuine political reform whose time has come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy' reads as the start of the sentence's mood, but it supplies the outer word, and 'that's now ready' is the definition, not commentary on the reform.
explanation.definitionFit: Something matured has ripened fully and is ready for use, like a cheese or wine.

clue.text: Change concerned with dance

parts.note: re means regarding or concerning
a jig is a lively dance

explanation.surface: Altering something to do with a folk dance.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejig is to rearrange or alter, a colloquial word for change.

clue.text: See what should be on plate by agreement

parts.note: lo is an old word for see or behold
a car number, shortened to car no, belongs on a number plate

explanation.surface: Looking at what is meant to be on your dinner plate by mutual consent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plate' suggests food, but it is a car's number plate.
explanation.definitionFit: The Locarno Treaties of 1925 were a European security pact, so the town's name stands for an agreement.

clue.text: See what's making the countryside rot in a bus twice

indicators.note: see invites the solver to look at what the following letters can make
twice means the phrase is used two times

explanation.surface: Look at what is turning the countryside rotten: a bus going through it again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram pool is ROT plus INABUS twice, fifteen letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Spreading suburbs build over open land, a loose description of the countryside being turned into housing.

clue.text: Lawbreaker in the beginning becomes stout fellow

indicators.note: in places the broken law inside the word for the beginning

parts.note: the beginning is the start
read as LAW broken: its letters rearranged give ALW

explanation.surface: A criminal starts out bad and ends up a solid citizen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lawbreaker' looks like a criminal, but it is LAW plus an anagram signal, giving ALW, which goes into START.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalwart is a loyal, sturdy supporter, a dependable stout fellow.

clue.text: 25 22's sheep have room

definitions.meaning: with 'have room' this evokes ... Room, a novel by Virginia Woolf
Jacob sheep are a piebald British breed

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads Woolf's Jacob's Room cut up as a sentence: the sheep of the breed named after the patriarch have room.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob sheep are a spotted breed, and Jacob's Room is the title of an early novel by the writer.

clue.text: See 23
Female poet holds small boy back from ground elder

parts.note: her is the female pronoun

indicators.note: holding something means having it inside, so the poet surrounds the boy

parts.note: a bard is a poet

indicators.note: back sends the short name the other way round

parts.note: Reg, short for Reginald, a boy's name in brief

explanation.surface: A woman poet keeps a little lad away from the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground elder' looks like a gardening phrase for the soil, but it is the name of a weed.
explanation.definitionFit: Herb Gerard is an old folk name for ground elder, the creeping garden weed.

clue.text: Medicine from tree manufactured in small limousine

indicators.note: something manufactured is put together anew, so these letters are reassembled

parts.note: limo is the shortened form of limousine

explanation.surface: A pharmaceutical made from a tree is produced in a compact luxury car.
explanation.definitionFit: Nim (neem) oil is pressed from the seeds of the neem tree and used medicinally.

clue.text: 25 22's married woman gets permit in time

indicators.note: in places the word for permit inside the period of time

parts.note: a day is a period of time
to permit is to allow

explanation.surface: Virginia Woolf's wife gets permission eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Dalloway is Woolf's novel; the married woman is the title's Mrs.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarissa Dalloway, the title character of Woolf's Mrs Dalloway, is a married society hostess.

clue.text: As corollary, journalist over American city dealt with clothes or money

indicators.note: as a corollary turns the statement round: if one thing is over another, the other is under it

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
the converse of over is under
ed is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: Consequently a reporter was posted to an American city and handled washing or dirty cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Journalist over city implies, as corollary, city under journalist: LA UNDER ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Laundered means washed, of clothes, or passed through legitimate channels, of illicit money.

clue.text: 25 22's time to cut birds

parts.note: to hew is to cut
Aves is the scientific class of birds

explanation.surface: In Woolf's book it is time to slaughter the birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The Waves is an experimental 1931 novel by the writer, told in six voices.

clue.text: Frank batsman in misery about rights and lefts

indicators.note: about means the misery word goes round the rights

parts.note: woe is misery
R twice for right, one per right
L twice for left

explanation.surface: A frank cricketer is miserable about his rights and lefts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like an adjective but is the first name of Sir Frank Worrell, the West Indies batsman and captain.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Frank Worrell was a great West Indian batsman and captain of the 1960s.

clue.text: Reduce silver work with hydrogen injection

indicators.note: an injection puts something inside, so the element goes into the reshaped metal
to work something is to shape it, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A metalworker shrinks silver by injecting hydrogen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges SILVER to SRIVEL, and the H goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrivel is to shrink and wrinkle, making something smaller.

clue.text: Boy that's scruffy and prickly

definitions.meaning: an old word for a hedgehog, and the spiny sea creature

explanation.definitionFit: A street urchin is a scruffy child; the hedgehog and sea urchin are both covered in spines.

clue.text: Decommission the person with the money

definitions.meaning: to dismiss an officer from the armed forces in disgrace
a bank or shop clerk handling cash

explanation.definitionFit: To cashier an officer is to discharge them; a cashier takes and pays out money in a bank or shop.

clue.text: Thora's pupil in promise to be developed

parts.note: Thora Hird, a much-loved British actress, read as T. Hird

indicators.note: in puts the learner inside the word for a pledge

parts.note: to give your word is to promise
L for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: An actress's student is pledged to be brought on.
explanation.walkthrough: Thora Hird was a British comic and character actress; her initial and surname give the first part.
explanation.definitionFit: The Third World is the old term for developing countries, those still to be developed.

clue.text: See 25
Wood strip makes bird a slut

parts.note: a slat is a thin strip of wood
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A thin piece of timber turns a bird into a loose woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A slattern is a dirty, untidy woman, an old insulting synonym.

clue.text: DJ produces poem with tenth note reversed

indicators.note: reversed turns the whole run of poem, numeral and note backwards

parts.note: an ode is a poem
X is the Roman numeral ten
ut is the old name for the note doh

explanation.surface: A disc jockey turns a poem round with a musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'DJ' looks like a disc jockey, but here it is a dinner jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: DJ is the British abbreviation for dinner jacket, which Americans call a tuxedo.

clue.text: State what beast sounds like whose fearfulness has been questioned

parts.note: Virginia is a US state

indicators.note: sounds like says the animal's name is heard, not written

parts.note: the beast is the wolf

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about an American state, an animal, and someone's courage.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the Albee play title Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Albee's play asks who is afraid of the novelist, so her fearfulness is literally a question.

clue.text: Ringer to turn into mad fly — I can't take any more!

parts.note: a bell is something that rings

indicators.note: into places the turn inside the jumbled insect
mad suggests the letters going wild

parts.note: U as in a U-turn

explanation.surface: A bell-ringer is driven to swat a frantic fly and cries out in exasperation.
explanation.definitionFit: To have had a bellyful is to be fed up, so the word stands for an exclamation of having had enough.

clue.text: In the course of … of the French and German cycle

parts.note: du is French for of the
Wagner's Ring cycle of German operas

explanation.surface: An unfinished phrase about something French and a German cycle race.
explanation.definitionFit: During means throughout or in the course of a period.
